I'm really sorry to hear that. It must be so hard to see someone you care about going through this. How are you holding up?
Honestly, I'm struggling. I want to help, but I'm scared of doing the wrong thing. It's like I'm walking on eggshells.
That sounds really challenging. It's natural to feel unsure, but your concern for Mark shows how much you care. Have you had a chance to talk to him or his doctors?
I haven't yet. I'm afraid of overwhelming him, or saying something that might upset him.
It's understandable to feel that way, but even just letting him know you're there for him can be very comforting. Sometimes just being present is a big support.
You're right. I keep thinking about everything else that's been going on, too. Like the issues at work and my anxiety shooting up lately. It's all piling up.
You've been through so much, especially with work stress and your personal life. It's okay to feel overwhelmed. Have you been able to talk about this with your therapist?
I have, but it's like nothing is changing fast enough. I started painting like they suggested and it helps, but only for a while.
It's good that you have that outlet. Sometimes progress feels slow, but every step counts. Maybe focusing on small victories can help lighten the load.
I guess I need to be more patient with myself. And with Mark, too. I just want to be able to support him without losing myself in the process.
Absolutely, maintaining your own well-being is crucial. Setting boundaries for yourself while being there for Mark is important. Have you thought about any ways to balance both?
I'm not sure. I think I'll start by reaching out to see how he is, then maybe discuss how we can keep in touch without it being overwhelming for either of us.
That sounds like a thoughtful approach. It's clear you care deeply, and by communicating openly, you can both find a comfortable dynamic.
Thanks for saying that. It's just hard feeling powerless in this situation, especially when someone you love is hurting.
It's a normal feeling, but you're doing what you can, and that matters. You're supportive and compassionate, and that will shine through for Mark.
I hope so. Thanks for being here to listen. It really means a lot to me.
I'm always here for you, Sarah. Don't hesitate to reach out whenever you need to talk.
Hey, I've been going through a lot lately and could really use someone to talk to.
Hi Sarah, I'm here for you. What's been on your mind?
Well, I've made a big decision to cut down on my working hours.
That's a significant step. How are you feeling about it?
It's a mix of relief and uncertainty. I'm glad to have more time for myself, but I worry about my career.
It's completely normal to feel both relieved and anxious. Taking care of your mental health is crucial though.
You're right. I've been trying to focus more on painting, as it helps with my stress.
That's wonderful. Engaging in a hobby can be so therapeutic. Have you noticed any changes in how you feel since you started painting?
Yes, definitely. It's like I can express what's inside without words, but sometimes the pressures of work still get to me.
It sounds like painting has become an important outlet for you. It's okay if work stress still creeps in; what matters is that you have ways to cope.
Thanks, I keep reminding myself of that. It's hard not to feel like I'm falling behind sometimes.
I understand. You've been through a lot with work and relationships. You're doing your best, and that's enough.
I try to remember that. The therapy sessions have helped too. I just worry about Mark being in the hospital; it brings back old anxieties.
It's tough seeing someone you care about struggle. Have you managed to talk to Mark or visit him?
I did visit him. It was really hard, but I think he appreciated the company. I just wish I could do more.
Sometimes being there is enough. You're a good friend, and your support means a lot to him.
Thanks. I just hope he knows that he's not alone.
I'm sure he does. Keep taking care of yourself too; you need your strength to support others.
I will. Cutting back on work is a start, I suppose.
It absolutely is. It's a brave decision, and shows you're prioritizing your well-being.
Sometimes I just doubt if I'm doing the right thing.
Doubt can be part of the process, but remember that prioritizing yourself isn't wrong.
I guess so. It's just that balancing everything feels overwhelming at times.
It's understandable. You're navigating a lot right now, but you're taking steps to manage it better.
Thanks for listening. I really needed to talk this through.
Anytime, Sarah. You're not alone in this, and don't hesitate to reach out whenever you need to.
Hey, do you have a minute? I could really use someone to talk to.
Of course, Sarah. What's on your mind?
Well, Jack and I are planning a weekend trip, and it's brought up a lot of feelings for me.
That sounds exciting, but it seems like there's more to it. What's been coming up for you?
Yeah, it's exciting, but I can't shake this anxiety. I'm worried about how we'll get along the whole time.
That makes sense, given the history between you two. Is there a specific aspect that's causing you concern?
I guess it's mainly about my need for personal space. We've had conflicts about that before.
I remember you mentioning how important independence is for you. Have you talked to Jack about your worries?
Not yet. I'm afraid it might turn into another argument.
It's understandable to feel hesitant. What about starting with a gentle conversation about expectations for the trip?
That's a good point. Setting expectations might help avoid misunderstandings.
Exactly. It's also a chance to reaffirm the importance of personal time, even during a getaway.
Yeah, I guess I'm just worried he won't understand. We've been good lately, and I don't want to ruin it.
It's natural to worry about that, but communicating your needs is important for both of you. He might appreciate your honesty.
You're right. I should trust that he cares enough to listen.
Absolutely. And remember, you're both growing through this. Have you thought about bringing some painting supplies to help relax during the trip?
I hadn't thought of that. It might be a nice way to have some personal time if needed.
Definitely. It could be a comforting space amidst the changes. And if things get overwhelming, it's okay to step back and regroup.
Thanks for reminding me. It's reassuring to know I have options.
You're welcome. Keep in mind that it's about enjoying the moment too. You'll be alright, Sarah.
Thanks, I really appreciate your support. It helps to talk it out and set things straight in my mind.
Hey, I could really use someone to talk to right now.
Of course, Sarah. What's been happening lately?
My parents just showed up unannounced, and it's really stressing me out.
That sounds unexpected. How are you coping with their visit?
It's been hard. They have so many questions about my life choices, and it's overwhelming.
It must be tough feeling pressured like that. Do you feel like they're not understanding where you're coming from?
Exactly. They don't understand why I've cut back on work hours or why I focus on my painting.
Your decisions are about taking care of your well-being, right? It's important they see how that's been positive for you.
Yes, but it's like they don't see my mental health as a good enough reason.
It's unfortunate they don't fully grasp the significance. How is this impacting your stress levels?
My anxiety is through the roof. It's like I'm back to feeling how I did during my breakdown last year.
I'm so sorry to hear that, Sarah. Have you been able to talk to your therapist about these feelings?
Not yet. My next session is in a few days. Meanwhile, I feel like I'm juggling so much at once.
It makes sense you'd feel that way. Between work, your relationship, and now this, it's a lot.
Yes, and I feel guilty for not being more patient with my parents. I know they mean well.
It must be hard balancing those feelings. It's okay to be kind to yourself in this situation.
Thank you. I'm trying to set some boundaries, but it's challenging.
That sounds like a constructive step forward. Is there a way you could express to them how painting and space have been healing for you?
I might try that. Maybe if they see how happy it makes me, they'll understand.
It's definitely worth a try. Let them see the positive impact it's had on your life.
I hope they see it too. I just want to find a way to enjoy their visit without it affecting my mental state too much.
That sounds like a healthy approach. Remember, you’re not alone in this—I'm here whenever you need to talk.
Thank you so much for listening. I already feel a bit better getting it off my chest.
Anytime, Sarah. Keep taking things one step at a time and reach out whenever you need more support.
I will. Thanks again for being here for me.
Hey, I'm really struggling today and could use someone to talk to.
Of course, Sarah. What's going on? I'm here for you.
I had a panic attack during a meeting at work today. It was horrible.
That sounds incredibly overwhelming. I'm sorry you had to experience that. Do you know what might've triggered it?
I think it's been building up for a while. Work's been really stressful, and I got some lukewarm feedback from my boss recently.
That makes sense. It sounds like a lot of pressure. Have you talked to your therapist about it?
Yeah, we've been working on stress management. I just felt a wave of panic today like everything was too much.
It’s understandable. Panic attacks can feel all-consuming. Have you considered what your work environment is doing to your well-being?
Definitely. Today made me seriously rethink my career path. I wonder if this job is right for me anymore.
That's a big realization. Have you thought about what you might want to pursue instead, or what changes might help?
I enjoy painting. It's my escape, and I started reducing my hours to focus more on personal projects. Maybe there's something there.
Pursuing something you love sounds refreshing. It could be a great way to balance out the stress from work.
Yeah, it's just that I've put so much into this career. It's hard to consider leaving it behind.
Change can be tough, especially when you've invested a lot into something. It's okay to take time to figure out what's best for you.
Thanks. My parents visited recently, and they didn't make it easier. They're worried about my lifestyle and choices.
That must add even more pressure. How do you feel about their concerns?
I know they mean well, but it just adds to my stress. I wish they could see my perspective and support me more.
It sounds like you’re navigating a lot right now. It's important to prioritize your mental health and happiness.
I agree. Maybe taking things one step at a time will help. I just need to breathe and reassess everything slowly.
That sounds like a healthy approach. You're doing the best you can, and that's enough.
Thank you. It helps to know I have someone to talk to about all this.
I'm always here for you, Sarah. Remember, you’re not alone in this.
Hey, I just really need to talk to someone.
Of course, Sarah. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
Things with Jack at work have been... difficult. It's affecting me a lot.
I'm sorry to hear that. It can be really challenging to balance a personal and professional relationship with a colleague. What happened?
We had an argument about work boundaries. It's like we can't separate our personal life from work, and it's creating tension.
That sounds really tough. Managing those boundaries can be incredibly difficult. Do you feel comfortable sharing more about the argument?
Well, it started when we disagreed on how to handle a project deadline. It spiraled into a discussion about giving each other space in our personal lives.
It seems like the work stress is seeping into your personal relationship. How are you feeling about it?
Honestly, I'm feeling really anxious. I don't want this to affect my work or my relationship with Jack, but it's hard to keep them separate.
It's completely understandable to feel anxious. You're trying to protect both aspects of your life. Have you had a chance to talk these feelings through with your therapist?
I mentioned it briefly, but our last session focused more on my panic attack during that work meeting. I haven't had the chance to dive deeper into this issue.
Panic attacks can be really overwhelming. It's great that you're able to work through these things with your therapist. Maybe discussing the situation with Jack could also be helpful?
Yeah, I think I need to have an open conversation with him. But I'm worried about how he'll react.
That's a valid concern, but it sounds like having that conversation might be an important step towards resolving some of this tension. How do you feel about planning when and how to talk to him?
I know it needs to happen, and it might help clear the air. Maybe I should suggest meeting outside of work so we can address it in a better setting.
Meeting outside of work sounds like a thoughtful approach. It could help create a neutral space. Remember to express your feelings and listen to his side too.
Thanks. I think setting some time aside this weekend could work. I'll try to remember to stay calm and focused during our talk.
You've got this, Sarah. You're taking steps towards improving your situation, and that's really commendable. How do you feel now about taking this step?
I feel a bit more relieved just talking about it and having a plan. I'll let you know how it goes.
Please do. I'm here if you need to talk again. Take care and good luck with the conversation.

current_prefix.text: Hey, do you have a moment to chat?
Of course, Kelly! What's on your mind?
I just found out that I didn't get the scholarship I applied for.
I'm so sorry to hear that. You must be really disappointed.
Yeah, it's just frustrating. I really thought this would be my chance to ease some of the financial pressures of grad school.
I can imagine. It's tough when you're expecting something that could make life a bit easier and it doesn't come through.
Exactly. And it just feels like a setback after working so hard, especially after everything with my thesis.
You've been through a lot recently, with the criticism on your thesis and the group project issues. It's okay to feel upset about this.
Thanks. I guess I just keep thinking about all the time and effort I put into the application. It feels like it's always something.
Your dedication is amazing, Kelly. Even if this didn’t work out, it doesn’t take away from all the effort you’ve put in.
It's hard to keep that perspective when these things happen back to back. It just adds to feeling stuck, you know?
Absolutely, and it's important to acknowledge that feeling. Have you thought about what you might do next?
I'm trying to keep my options open. There's the internship offer, but I'm not sure about committing to it right now.
It's understandable to feel conflicted. The internship could be a valuable experience, but it's okay to take your time deciding.
I appreciate you saying that. I guess I'll think on it more after this initial disappointment passes.
That's a healthy approach, Kelly. It's important to give yourself space to process everything.
Thanks for listening and for understanding. It's comforting to have someone to talk to about this.

turns.text: Hey Kelly, how are you doing today?
Hey, to be honest, I'm struggling a bit.
I'm here to listen. Do you want to share what's been challenging for you?
It's my thesis. I had a setback recently, and it's just really bringing me down.
I can imagine that must be tough. What happened with your thesis?
I got some feedback that I wasn't expecting. It made me realize there's a lot more work to do than I thought.
That sounds overwhelming. It can be really hard to digest unexpected feedback.
Exactly. I was feeling quite confident before, and now I just feel lost.
It's okay to feel that way. Remember, feedback is part of the process. How are you managing these feelings?
Not too well, honestly. I've been pretty demotivated and haven't been able to get much done.
It's understandable to feel stuck. Sometimes taking a step back can help. Have you tried taking a break from it all?
I've tried, but it's hard not to think about it. It feels like I'm letting myself down.
You're not letting yourself down. You're doing your best under challenging circumstances. Remember when your friend mentioned overcoming similar doubts in his studies?
Oh yeah, he struggled with something similar and he got through it. It took him a bit of time though.
Exactly. Maybe his story can be a reminder that it's possible to bounce back. Have you reached out to your friends recently?
Not recently. Maybe I should. Talking to someone who understands might help.
That sounds like a great idea. And remember, I'm always here for you too. You have support.
Thanks, I really appreciate that. It does help to know I'm not alone in this.
You definitely aren't alone. How about focusing on one small step you can take today?
Maybe I can start by reviewing the feedback more calmly, with a fresh perspective.
That sounds like a constructive plan. Taking it step by step and being kind to yourself on the journey can make a big difference.
I’ll try to keep that in mind. Thank you for listening and helping me process things.
Anytime, Kelly. You’ve got this, even if it doesn’t feel like it right now. Keep reaching out, okay?
I will. Thanks again.
Hello
Hi, how are you feeling today?
I'm feeling a bit confused and anxious.
okay, that is valid, do you have an idea what is causing the confusion?

So I've been dating and my parents are aware. But recently after I said I want to go on a trip with my boyfriend, my parents have all sorts of opinions about it. And all their traditional beliefs that I did not know existed are now on the surface and they are kinda forcing me to follow it.
For say they think "bad types of woman" go on trips with their boyfriends and I need to save myself.
They have been guilt tripping me and I feel very confused.
Your feelings are valid and it is okay to feel confused in this situation considering you love your boyfriend and parents
Have you tried discussing with your boyfriend to talk to your parents as a means of reassuring them?
Or getting someone neutral that your parents trust to talk to them?

I have. It's been a long stressful month of discussion. The problem is I don't share their beliefs, and I haven't been really "saving myself". I'm been living away from them for collage quite a while and I've been basically doing stuff that if they found out they would be very upset about.
But I didn't think it bothers them because they never shared any of this.
And they said if I go on this trip I'm disrespecting them and the entire family.
But his parents are totally cool and don't seem to mind.

I get how difficult and upsetting this situation is to you, i have been in a similar situation, however, in my case i took charge of my life, though they are my parents i did what i felt is good for me
Before i continue, do you mind me asking how old you are?
I'm 26
And I see what you're saying.
It's really hard breaking free because they always monitored me my entire life.
I never had a voice for myself. They basically bullied and forced me to do what they wanted.
BTW if you didn't guess I'm their favorite child.
Okay, you are old enough to be away from your parents, i am going to suggest you sitting with them down and having a heart to heart discussion with them
Let them know the consequences of them forcing you, your feelings towards it and how unhappy you are with them restricting you
Should I tell them everything I did that goes against what they believe?
So they know that I don't share their beliefs?
No, i think that should be personal to you, i would not suggest you hurting or making them see you as a disappointment
I am sure you will be fine after discussing with them, they will come around
I guess worst case I won't talk to them for a while : )
Thank you , that helped.
They might be sad and upset now but they will get over it definitely
You are welcome
Have a good one!
You too
How is your feeling now?
I have mixed feelings sad and angry at the same time.
It seems that you are feeling blue and upset by others, right?
Yes. Am sad because I love my mom so much and I never like to get into arguments with her.
From the short conversation, I can feel how sad you are.
Yes. My mom never approves of most of the things I do.
What kind of arguments did you have with your mom?
Like the kind of friends I should have. I believe I have freedom to choose my friends not her.
I had similar situation like yours. My mom did not want me to make friends with some people.
Really? How did you deal with that because for me it makes me angry.
I just had good conversations with my mom to express my thoughts. Did you have a frank chat with your mom to express your concerns?
I try to but it never ends well if I don't agree with her suggestions.
Take a deep breath and it can make you feel better.
What are her concerns about your friends?
OK! I have taken a deep breath.
ok, that's good. tell me more about your mom's concerns of your friends.
She feels that they have some bad influence on me because of their family background. I don't do anything bad with them.
Some of my friends are so good they even inspire me to be better everyday.
My mom told me similar concerns before. It is understandable.
All I need is to find a way to show her that I can make some good decisions as well and that she can trust me to make good friends. I have never gotten into trouble before with my friends
My suggestion is that tell her these facts and she can make a better decision. I think she assumed your friends are bad influencers just based on their family background.
Do I need to buy her a gift or something to let her know I care so as to start the conversation?
Yes, a good idea, it pleases her.
Thank you for your time.
Bye
You are welcome. Hope it will go well.
Hi there, how is this season treating you?
It's alright. Definitely not as cold as last year which is something to be slightly thankful for.
Well let's be grateful for small mercies :). How are you feeling in yourself though? Is there anything you'd like to talk about?
I'm worried about grad school
Ah I am sorry to hear that. Please try not to worry too much as it's a common worry to have. Do you want to tell me the details?

Sure. One of my classes is extremely difficult and the professor has not been responsive at all. The TA is kind enough to make time to help me with homework, but my grades are still not great. It makes me feel really dumb and undeserving to be in that class
So you are feeling as though you are in the wrong place? Do you feel as though you might fail your class completely?

I want to be in the program, it's just that I feel like everyone is so much smarter than me and my performance in that class makes me question my admission into the programs sometimes. When I feel like this after submitting homework, I end up crying because I just want to do well. I enjoy this field, just not this  class in particular.
I'm afraid of failing, but I'm not sure if that should be a concern either. Over the past 3 years, no one has gotten a grade lower than a B.
But do you really think that you would have been admitted to the class if you were not up to the standard? Do you think that maybe most of your classmates are secretly feeling the same?
Sometimes I think about that. At the same time, I feel like it's unfair to compare myself to others.
This sounds like it might be a self esteem issue and not about your grades. I have felt this sort of thing myself and I do know how awful it is to be so hard on yourself.
So what do I do about it? I don't want to keep feeling like this
Have you thought about seeing a therapist? Does your school have any free therapy programmes you could use?

I don't think my school has free therapy programs. I have thought about seeing a therapist but I've heard therapy is very expensive.With student loans, I didn't really put much more research into therapy past hearing about the costs.
A far as I am aware there are charitable organisations which can arrange a few free therapy session for you. Perhaps you could talk to your doctor about it?
I have had free therapy sessions before and I found them very helpful
I think free therapy sessions would be a good place to start
It would help you work on your self confidence and you might find that you are not doing as badly in school as you think you are.
Yeah, there are definitely a lot of other things i'm insecure about
Then I think it is probably just a general self esteem issue and nothing academic!
Anyway it's been really nice to talk to you and I hope that everything goes your way
I think talking about this has helped. I'll do a little more digging. Thank you!
You're most welcome, have a lovely Holiday season.
Hey, I really need to talk to someone.
Hi Kelly! Of course, I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
I got into an argument today with a classmate during our group project meeting. I'm feeling so overwhelmed.
I'm sorry to hear that. It sounds really stressful. What happened in the argument?
We were discussing some decisions for the project, and they just dismissed my ideas completely. It made me feel invisible and undervalued.
That must have been so frustrating. Everyone's contributions should be respected, especially in a group setting.
Exactly. It's like, what am I even doing here if no one will listen.
I can understand why that would make you question your place in the group. Did you manage to express how you felt to them?
Sort of. I tried, but I think I let my emotions get the better of me and it just turned into more arguing. Now I'm worried I've damaged the group dynamic.
Sometimes emotions can take over, especially when you're feeling undervalued. It's understandable. Have you thought about how you might address it with them?
I want to approach them again and explain. But I'm worried they'll just see it as me being difficult or emotional.
It's brave of you to want to reach out again. Maybe approaching them calmly and expressing how the situation made you feel could help clear the air.
Yeah, I think I'll try that. I guess I'm also feeling extra sensitive lately because of that difficult class I'm taking.
Having a tough class on top of this situation is a lot. It's no wonder you're feeling sensitive. How is that going for you?
It's intense. I'm constantly worried I'm falling behind, and it's really impacting my self-esteem.
That's tough. Balancing a challenging class with group dynamics can be overwhelming. Remember, it's okay to feel this way.
Thank you. I've been considering therapy to help with these feelings and to improve my self-esteem.
That sounds like a positive step. Taking care of your mental health is important, especially during stressful times.
I'm glad you think so. I just hope it can help me manage everything better.
I'm confident it will. You're taking the first steps towards understanding and improving your situation, and that's truly commendable.
Thank you. It really helps to hear that and to talk to you.
Anytime, Kelly. I'm always here to support you. You've got this, even when it feels challenging.
I appreciate it more than you know. I guess I'll focus on clearing the air with my classmate and seeking therapy.
That sounds like a great plan. Remember, you're stronger than you think, and you're not alone in this.
Hey Kelly, how are you feeling about your thesis presentation coming up?
Hey! Honestly, I'm feeling pretty anxious about it.
I'm sorry to hear that. What's been making you feel anxious?
I guess it’s the pressure of it all. My thesis is such a big part of my degree, and I really don't want to mess it up.
That makes a lot of sense, it's a big moment. Remember how you pulled through the setback earlier this year with your thesis?
Yeah, I remember. It was tough, but I managed. This feels different, though. It's like everyone will be watching and judging.
Presentations can definitely feel intimidating. It's perfectly normal to feel that way. Do you think there are specific parts of the presentation that you're worried about?
I think I’m most worried about the Q&A part. I'm scared I won't be able to answer their questions, and it will look like I don’t understand my own research.
That’s a common fear. Maybe we can go over some possible questions together and practice? It might help boost your confidence.
That sounds like a good idea. It would help to be more prepared for the unexpected.
Great! And remember, you know your work better than anyone else. It’s normal to get caught off guard, but you've got this.
Thanks, I appreciate that. I guess a part of me also wonders if people will even find my research interesting.
Your research is your unique contribution. It's meaningful and valuable. Don't underestimate the impact it can have.
I try to keep that in mind, but the doubt just keeps creeping in, you know?
I understand. Doubt is tough. Maybe reflecting on why you started this research in the first place might help?
I started it because I wanted to make a difference, and I was passionate about the topic. I guess I’ve lost sight of that a little.
Reconnecting with that original passion can be a powerful motivator. It's still there, even if it feels lost right now.
Yeah, it's reassuring to remember that. I don't want a repeat of that project argument from September either.
I remember you mentioning that. It was a difficult situation, but you handled it well in the end. You grew from that experience.
I did, didn't I? It's just hard to see it sometimes. Thanks for reminding me.
Anytime. You're stronger and more capable than you give yourself credit for. Just take one step at a time.
I will. Thanks for being here and listening to me vent.
I'm always here for you. We can practice the Q&A whenever you're ready.
That’d be great. I’ll reach out soon to set up a time. Thanks again!
Hey, do you have a moment to chat?
Of course, Kelly. What's on your mind?
I had my thesis presentation yesterday, and it didn't go as I hoped.
I'm so sorry to hear that. Can you tell me what happened?
Well, I was really nervous from the start. I tried to stay calm, but I stumbled over my words.
That sounds really stressful. It’s tough when things don’t go as planned.
Yeah, and the Q&A session was even worse. I struggled to answer some of the questions.
It must have been nerve-wracking. But remember, it's okay not to have all the answers. Everyone has challenging presentations.
I know, but I feel like I should have been more prepared. This presentation was really important for my progression.
It's understandable to feel disappointed, especially when you care so much about your work.
Thank you. I just keep thinking about how everyone was watching, and it's hard not to dwell on every little mistake.
It’s natural to replay moments like this, but be gentle with yourself. You're doing the best you can.
I appreciate that. I just wish I could prove that I know my stuff, even if this didn’t show it.
You are knowledgeable, and this one presentation doesn't define your abilities.
It's been a rough month, between this and the argument over that group project.
You've been dealing with a lot lately. No wonder you're feeling overwhelmed.
I guess I just need to find a way to bounce back and regain some confidence.
Rebuilding confidence takes time, but remember how resilient you were after your last thesis setback.
True, I did manage to push through back then. Maybe I can do it again.
Absolutely! Lean on your past strength, and know I'm here for support whenever you need.
Thank you. It really helps to talk it out and get some reassurance.
I'm glad I can be here for you. You're not alone in this.
Thanks. I'll try to keep that in mind and take it one step at a time.
That sounds like a good plan. You've got this, Kelly.
Hey, have a moment to chat?
Of course, Kelly. What's on your mind?
I've been feeling a bit off ever since the presentation.
I'm really sorry to hear that. Do you want to share more about what happened?
The presentation didn't go as I planned, and the Q&A was even worse.
That must have been really challenging. It's understandable to feel disappointed.
Yeah, it's just this lingering feeling of having let myself down.
It's tough to cope with those feelings, especially when you've worked so hard.
My friend invited me to a yoga retreat. I think it's her way of helping me unwind.
That sounds like a thoughtful gesture. A change of scenery and some relaxation could be beneficial.
I'm just not sure if it'll help or if it's running away from my problems.
It's completely okay to take some time for yourself. Recharging doesn't mean avoiding the problem.
I guess a break might give me a fresh perspective when I come back.
Absolutely. Sometimes stepping away helps in seeing things more clearly.
I've been so caught up in trying to perfect everything, maybe too much.
It's easy to fall into that trap. Remember, it's okay to have moments that aren't perfect.
I appreciate you saying that. I tend to forget it's okay to not always meet high expectations.
It's important to be kind to yourself. You've accomplished so much already.
You're right, I need to remind myself of that more often.
Yes, and don't hesitate to lean on your friends or me whenever you need support.

Thank you. I really appreciate that. I'll keep working on taking those small steps.
That's a great approach. I'm proud of you for tackling things one step at a time.
Thank you. I'll keep you posted on how everything goes.
Please do. Take care, Sarah. You've got this.
Hey, I really need to talk. Got a moment?
Of course, Sarah. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
I had my performance review yesterday, and it didn't go as well as I hoped.
I'm sorry to hear that. What did your boss say?
She said my work was 'adequate,' but I was hoping for something more positive.
It's tough not getting the feedback you were expecting, especially when you put in so much effort.
Yeah, it just made me question if I'm even doing a good job.
It's understandable that you're feeling this way. This doesn't define your worth or capabilities.
I know, but after the whole incident with my old boss, I'm just on edge about everything.
That was such a difficult time for you. It's normal for these feelings to resurface.
And I keep thinking about how my friend is doing. I don't want to burden them with my stuff.
You're such a caring person, Sarah. It's okay to focus on yourself too.
Thanks, I just hope this doesn't affect my relationship with Jack. We've had our ups and downs.
Remember, Jack cares about you a lot. It's important to communicate how you're feeling.
I think I'll talk to him tonight. Being open seems to help us a lot.
That sounds like a great idea. How about the painting hobby you started? Is that helping?
It does help. It's nice to have a creative outlet, even if it's just for a bit.
That's wonderful to hear. Taking time for yourself can really make a difference.
Yeah, I just have to remind myself of that. Thank you for listening and just being here.
Anytime, Sarah. I'm really proud of how you're handling everything.
That means a lot. I'll try to take things one step at a time.
Exactly. You've got this, and I'm always here if you need to talk.
Hey, I really need to talk.
Of course, Sarah. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
It's about Mark... he was hospitalized recently due to his mental health. I feel so helpless and worried.
I'm really sorry to hear that. It must be so hard to see someone you care about going through this. How are you holding up?
Honestly, I'm struggling. I want to help, but I'm scared of doing the wrong thing. It's like I'm walking on eggshells.
That sounds really challenging. It's natural to feel unsure, but your concern for Mark shows how much you care. Have you had a chance to talk to him or his doctors?
I haven't yet. I'm afraid of overwhelming him, or saying something that might upset him.
It's understandable to feel that way, but even just letting him know you're there for him can be very comforting. Sometimes just being present is a big support.
You're right. I keep thinking about everything else that's been going on, too. Like the issues at work and my anxiety shooting up lately. It's all piling up.
You've been through so much, especially with work stress and your personal life. It's okay to feel overwhelmed. Have you been able to talk about this with your therapist?
I have, but it's like nothing is changing fast enough. I started painting like they suggested and it helps, but only for a while.
It's good that you have that outlet. Sometimes progress feels slow, but every step counts. Maybe focusing on small victories can help lighten the load.
I guess I need to be more patient with myself. And with Mark, too. I just want to be able to support him without losing myself in the process.
Absolutely, maintaining your own well-being is crucial. Setting boundaries for yourself while being there for Mark is important. Have you thought about any ways to balance both?
I'm not sure. I think I'll start by reaching out to see how he is, then maybe discuss how we can keep in touch without it being overwhelming for either of us.
That sounds like a thoughtful approach. It's clear you care deeply, and by communicating openly, you can both find a comfortable dynamic.
Thanks for saying that. It's just hard feeling powerless in this situation, especially when someone you love is hurting.
It's a normal feeling, but you're doing what you can, and that matters. You're supportive and compassionate, and that will shine through for Mark.
I hope so. Thanks for being here to listen. It really means a lot to me.
I'm always here for you, Sarah. Don't hesitate to reach out whenever you need to talk.
Hey, I've been going through a lot lately and could really use someone to talk to.
Hi Sarah, I'm here for you. What's been on your mind?
Well, I've made a big decision to cut down on my working hours.
That's a significant step. How are you feeling about it?
It's a mix of relief and uncertainty. I'm glad to have more time for myself, but I worry about my career.
It's completely normal to feel both relieved and anxious. Taking care of your mental health is crucial though.
You're right. I've been trying to focus more on painting, as it helps with my stress.
That's wonderful. Engaging in a hobby can be so therapeutic. Have you noticed any changes in how you feel since you started painting?
Yes, definitely. It's like I can express what's inside without words, but sometimes the pressures of work still get to me.
It sounds like painting has become an important outlet for you. It's okay if work stress still creeps in; what matters is that you have ways to cope.
Thanks, I keep reminding myself of that. It's hard not to feel like I'm falling behind sometimes.
I understand. You've been through a lot with work and relationships. You're doing your best, and that's enough.
I try to remember that. The therapy sessions have helped too. I just worry about Mark being in the hospital; it brings back old anxieties.
It's tough seeing someone you care about struggle. Have you managed to talk to Mark or visit him?
I did visit him. It was really hard, but I think he appreciated the company. I just wish I could do more.
Sometimes being there is enough. You're a good friend, and your support means a lot to him.
Thanks. I just hope he knows that he's not alone.
I'm sure he does. Keep taking care of yourself too; you need your strength to support others.
I will. Cutting back on work is a start, I suppose.
It absolutely is. It's a brave decision, and shows you're prioritizing your well-being.
Sometimes I just doubt if I'm doing the right thing.
Doubt can be part of the process, but remember that prioritizing yourself isn't wrong.
I guess so. It's just that balancing everything feels overwhelming at times.
It's understandable. You're navigating a lot right now, but you're taking steps to manage it better.
Thanks for listening. I really needed to talk this through.
Anytime, Sarah. You're not alone in this, and don't hesitate to reach out whenever you need to.
Hey, do you have a minute? I could really use someone to talk to.
Of course, Sarah. What's on your mind?
Well, Jack and I are planning a weekend trip, and it's brought up a lot of feelings for me.
That sounds exciting, but it seems like there's more to it. What's been coming up for you?
Yeah, it's exciting, but I can't shake this anxiety. I'm worried about how we'll get along the whole time.
That makes sense, given the history between you two. Is there a specific aspect that's causing you concern?
I guess it's mainly about my need for personal space. We've had conflicts about that before.
I remember you mentioning how important independence is for you. Have you talked to Jack about your worries?
Not yet. I'm afraid it might turn into another argument.
It's understandable to feel hesitant. What about starting with a gentle conversation about expectations for the trip?
That's a good point. Setting expectations might help avoid misunderstandings.
Exactly. It's also a chance to reaffirm the importance of personal time, even during a getaway.
Yeah, I guess I'm just worried he won't understand. We've been good lately, and I don't want to ruin it.
It's natural to worry about that, but communicating your needs is important for both of you. He might appreciate your honesty.
You're right. I should trust that he cares enough to listen.
Absolutely. And remember, you're both growing through this. Have you thought about bringing some painting supplies to help relax during the trip?
I hadn't thought of that. It might be a nice way to have some personal time if needed.
Definitely. It could be a comforting space amidst the changes. And if things get overwhelming, it's okay to step back and regroup.
Thanks for reminding me. It's reassuring to know I have options.
You're welcome. Keep in mind that it's about enjoying the moment too. You'll be alright, Sarah.
Thanks, I really appreciate your support. It helps to talk it out and set things straight in my mind.
Hey, I could really use someone to talk to right now.
Of course, Sarah. What's been happening lately?
My parents just showed up unannounced, and it's really stressing me out.
That sounds unexpected. How are you coping with their visit?
It's been hard. They have so many questions about my life choices, and it's overwhelming.
It must be tough feeling pressured like that. Do you feel like they're not understanding where you're coming from?
Exactly. They don't understand why I've cut back on work hours or why I focus on my painting.
Your decisions are about taking care of your well-being, right? It's important they see how that's been positive for you.
Yes, but it's like they don't see my mental health as a good enough reason.
It's unfortunate they don't fully grasp the significance. How is this impacting your stress levels?
My anxiety is through the roof. It's like I'm back to feeling how I did during my breakdown last year.
I'm so sorry to hear that, Sarah. Have you been able to talk to your therapist about these feelings?
Not yet. My next session is in a few days. Meanwhile, I feel like I'm juggling so much at once.
It makes sense you'd feel that way. Between work, your relationship, and now this, it's a lot.
Yes, and I feel guilty for not being more patient with my parents. I know they mean well.
It must be hard balancing those feelings. It's okay to be kind to yourself in this situation.
Thank you. I'm trying to set some boundaries, but it's challenging.
That sounds like a constructive step forward. Is there a way you could express to them how painting and space have been healing for you?
I might try that. Maybe if they see how happy it makes me, they'll understand.
It's definitely worth a try. Let them see the positive impact it's had on your life.
I hope they see it too. I just want to find a way to enjoy their visit without it affecting my mental state too much.
That sounds like a healthy approach. Remember, you’re not alone in this—I'm here whenever you need to talk.
Thank you so much for listening. I already feel a bit better getting it off my chest.
Anytime, Sarah. Keep taking things one step at a time and reach out whenever you need more support.
I will. Thanks again for being here for me.
Hey, I'm really struggling today and could use someone to talk to.
Of course, Sarah. What's going on? I'm here for you.
I had a panic attack during a meeting at work today. It was horrible.
That sounds incredibly overwhelming. I'm sorry you had to experience that. Do you know what might've triggered it?
I think it's been building up for a while. Work's been really stressful, and I got some lukewarm feedback from my boss recently.
That makes sense. It sounds like a lot of pressure. Have you talked to your therapist about it?
Yeah, we've been working on stress management. I just felt a wave of panic today like everything was too much.
It’s understandable. Panic attacks can feel all-consuming. Have you considered what your work environment is doing to your well-being?
Definitely. Today made me seriously rethink my career path. I wonder if this job is right for me anymore.
That's a big realization. Have you thought about what you might want to pursue instead, or what changes might help?
I enjoy painting. It's my escape, and I started reducing my hours to focus more on personal projects. Maybe there's something there.
Pursuing something you love sounds refreshing. It could be a great way to balance out the stress from work.
Yeah, it's just that I've put so much into this career. It's hard to consider leaving it behind.
Change can be tough, especially when you've invested a lot into something. It's okay to take time to figure out what's best for you.
Thanks. My parents visited recently, and they didn't make it easier. They're worried about my lifestyle and choices.
That must add even more pressure. How do you feel about their concerns?
I know they mean well, but it just adds to my stress. I wish they could see my perspective and support me more.
It sounds like you’re navigating a lot right now. It's important to prioritize your mental health and happiness.
I agree. Maybe taking things one step at a time will help. I just need to breathe and reassess everything slowly.
That sounds like a healthy approach. You're doing the best you can, and that's enough.
Thank you. It helps to know I have someone to talk to about all this.
I'm always here for you, Sarah. Remember, you’re not alone in this.
Hey, I just really need to talk to someone.
Of course, Sarah. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
Things with Jack at work have been... difficult. It's affecting me a lot.
I'm sorry to hear that. It can be really challenging to balance a personal and professional relationship with a colleague. What happened?
We had an argument about work boundaries. It's like we can't separate our personal life from work, and it's creating tension.
That sounds really tough. Managing those boundaries can be incredibly difficult. Do you feel comfortable sharing more about the argument?
Well, it started when we disagreed on how to handle a project deadline. It spiraled into a discussion about giving each other space in our personal lives.
It seems like the work stress is seeping into your personal relationship. How are you feeling about it?
Honestly, I'm feeling really anxious. I don't want this to affect my work or my relationship with Jack, but it's hard to keep them separate.
It's completely understandable to feel anxious. You're trying to protect both aspects of your life. Have you had a chance to talk these feelings through with your therapist?
I mentioned it briefly, but our last session focused more on my panic attack during that work meeting. I haven't had the chance to dive deeper into this issue.
Panic attacks can be really overwhelming. It's great that you're able to work through these things with your therapist. Maybe discussing the situation with Jack could also be helpful?
Yeah, I think I need to have an open conversation with him. But I'm worried about how he'll react.
That's a valid concern, but it sounds like having that conversation might be an important step towards resolving some of this tension. How do you feel about planning when and how to talk to him?
I know it needs to happen, and it might help clear the air. Maybe I should suggest meeting outside of work so we can address it in a better setting.
Meeting outside of work sounds like a thoughtful approach. It could help create a neutral space. Remember to express your feelings and listen to his side too.
Thanks. I think setting some time aside this weekend could work. I'll try to remember to stay calm and focused during our talk.
You've got this, Sarah. You're taking steps towards improving your situation, and that's really commendable. How do you feel now about taking this step?
I feel a bit more relieved just talking about it and having a plan. I'll let you know how it goes.
Please do. I'm here if you need to talk again. Take care and good luck with the conversation.
Hey, do you have a moment to chat?
Of course, Sarah. What's going on?
I've just been feeling a bit anxious lately, especially about starting this new blog on mental health.
That sounds like a big step. What makes you feel anxious about it?
I worry that I'm not experienced enough to speak on such important topics or that no one will relate to my experiences.
It's completely normal to have doubts when starting something new. But from what I know, you've been through quite a lot, which can give you a deep understanding of mental health.
True... I guess part of me feels that by sharing my journey, it might help others, but I feel vulnerable being so open.
Vulnerability takes courage, and it can be incredibly powerful. Have you thought about the positive impact your story could have on others?
Yes, I think back to my breakdown at work and how isolated I felt. If I can prevent someone else from feeling that way, it would be worth it.
That's an amazing motivation, Sarah. It sounds like your blog could serve as a source of solace for many.
Thank you. I just hope I can express everything clearly. Sometimes, I get overwhelmed with everything I want to say.
What if you start by writing about one experience at a time? It might make it easier to focus and build the blog gradually.
I like that idea. Maybe starting with big moments like dealing with work stress or my anxiety attacks could set a strong foundation.
That sounds like a good plan. Remember how your therapist suggested taking things step by step when managing stress? This can apply here too.
Yes, that's true. Breaking it down into smaller parts seems more manageable.
And don't forget, you're doing this not just for others but for yourself as well. It sounds like it could be a therapeutic outlet for you.
I think so too. Writing has always been a way for me to process my thoughts and feelings. Maybe this is just what I need right now.
Exactly. Plus, the responses and connections you'll make through your blog could provide new perspectives on your journey.
I hadn't thought about that. Engaging with others could definitely expand my understanding.
And if ever you need to vent or bounce ideas around, I'm here to listen. You're taking a brave step forward, and that's something to be proud of.
Thank you. I really appreciate your support. I'll keep you posted on my progress.
Looking forward to seeing your journey unfold, Sarah. You've got this.
Hey Sarah, it's good to see you here. How have you been feeling lately?
Hi, it's been a bit rough. I had an anxiety attack recently after an argument with Jack about our future.
I'm so sorry to hear that. Can you tell me more about what led to the argument?
We've been talking about future plans, and I just started feeling overwhelmed. There are a lot of changes, and it spiraled into this fight.
Change can definitely be tough. It sounds like you're dealing with quite a bit all at once. What changes are you most concerned about?
I think it's mostly the idea of committing to bigger plans like moving in together or even career changes. It feels so permanent and I'm scared of making the wrong decision.
Those are huge decisions, and it's natural to feel apprehensive. It's important that you feel ready. Have you been able to discuss these fears with Jack?
Not really, the conversation usually turns into a debate instead of a discussion. It's like we're on different pages sometimes.
I can understand how frustrating that must be. Communication is key, but it's also hard to stay calm during intense discussions. Do you think setting aside time to talk would help?
I think it might. I'm just worried that my fears will be dismissed again, and I don't want to feel that way anymore.
It's important that both of you feel heard. Maybe framing it as a series of conversations rather than a one-time talk might help ease the pressure.
That's a good point. Maybe if we take it slow, I won't feel as anxious. I just hate feeling like I'm holding things up.
You’re not holding anything up by wanting to make thoughtful decisions. It's important to move at a pace that feels right for you. Have you reached out to your therapist about these feelings?
Yeah, I'm seeing them tomorrow. They've been helpful, especially since I started painting.
That's great to hear. Painting sounds like a wonderful outlet for you. Have you found it helps with processing these emotions?
It really does. It's like a form of meditation for me. It gives me the space to think things through away from all the noise.
It’s wonderful you have an outlet like that. It’s important to have those moments of reflection. Is there anything else that's been weighing on you recently?
I guess I'm still feeling pressure from work. Even though I'm working fewer hours, the expectations feel as high as ever.
That sounds really challenging. It's hard when expectations don't align with capacity. Have you been able to communicate your boundaries to your boss?
I have, but it's almost like they nod, agree, and then nothing changes. I'm worried about my performance reviews.

It must be frustrating to feel unheard at work. Staying true to your boundaries is really important. Do you think there’s a way to document these discussions with your boss so there’s a record of your concerns?
That's a good idea. I think having it written down might help. At least it would make me feel like actions are being taken.
It's always worth a try, and it might give you some peace of mind knowing there's a trail. Remember, taking care of your mental health is just as important as your career, if not more.
Thank you for saying that. I tend to forget sometimes. This whole conversation has made me feel lighter.
I'm really glad to hear that, Sarah. Remember, you’re doing a fantastic job navigating all these challenges. You’re stronger than you give yourself credit for.
Thank you for being here and listening. It means a lot to know I have someone to talk to.
Anytime, Sarah. I'm here whenever you need to talk. Take care of yourself.
Hey, thanks for being here. I could really use someone to listen right now.
Of course, Sarah. I'm here for you. What's been on your mind?
It's been a lot lately. My therapist suggested mindfulness exercises to help with my anxiety.
Mindfulness can be really helpful. How are you finding it so far?
Honestly, I haven't started yet. I feel kind of overwhelmed by everything else.
That's understandable. Sometimes starting something new can add to the stress. What's been overwhelming you the most?
Well, there was that argument with Jack about our future plans. It left me feeling really unsettled.
It's tough when future plans aren't aligning. Do you want to share more about the argument?
We were talking about moving in together and it kind of spiraled from there. I guess I'm scared of losing my independence.
It's natural to feel that way. Balancing a relationship and personal space can be challenging. Have you been able to discuss these concerns with him since the argument?
Not really. It feels like we both need some space to process things first.
Taking time to process can be wise. Maybe mindfulness could help you sort through these emotions too?
I suppose it could, but I'm also distracted by work stress. My boss's feedback hasn't been as encouraging as I hoped.
I'm sorry to hear that. It can be discouraging when hard work isn't recognized. Did the feedback touch on anything specific?
It was more general, but it left me feeling inadequate, like I'm not meeting expectations.
Feeling inadequate can be really tough, especially when you're already dealing with so much. Remember, you've handled difficult situations before.
That's true. I've come this far, and I guess a part of me knows I can handle this too. But I can't help but feel stuck sometimes.
Feeling stuck is a common experience, especially with so many pressures. Maybe pinpointing small steps could help ease that feeling?
Small steps could work. My therapist did mention focusing on manageable goals, like starting with one mindfulness session a day.
That sounds like a great first step. Even small progress can bring a sense of accomplishment and relief.
Thanks for reminding me of that. I want to believe it'll get better. Perhaps I'll try a mindfulness session tonight.
That's a positive move. Remember, I'm here anytime you want to talk or share how it's going.
Thank you. It really helps to have someone to confide in. I appreciate you being here for me.
It's my pleasure. You're doing your best, and that's what matters most. Take care of yourself, Sarah.
Hey, are you around? I could use someone to talk to.
Hi Sarah, I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
It's about Jack... We've decided to take a break.
That sounds tough, especially with everything you've shared about your relationship struggles.
Yeah, it was kind of expected but still hurts.
It's normal to feel that way. Do you want to talk more about what led to the decision?
I think everything just built up over time. The work stress, personal space issues... It all became too much.
That's understandable. It sounds like there were a lot of pressures from different areas.
Yeah, and with his role being part of my work life too, it complicates things further.
Having that overlap can add another layer of stress. How are you coping with this?
Honestly, I'm not sure. I've been trying to immerse myself in painting, as my therapist suggested.
Painting sounds like a great outlet. I'm glad you have something like that to turn to.
It's been helping, but the anxiety is still there, especially after recent arguments.
Have the mindfulness exercises from your therapist been helpful at all?
They help a bit. I just feel overwhelmed sometimes, like I'm juggling too many things.
It sounds like you have a lot on your plate. Remember to be kind to yourself during this time.
I'm trying. It's just hard sometimes, especially with all these changes.
Change can be daunting, but it's also an opportunity for growth. I'm here for you every step of the way.
Thank you, it means a lot. It feels good to have someone to talk to.
You're not alone, Sarah. We'll get through this together.
I know. It's comforting to have a support system.
Absolutely. If you ever feel like you're slipping, whether it's about Jack or anything else, just reach out.
I will. For now, I think I'll focus on painting a bit more this weekend.
That sounds like a perfect plan. Let the creativity flow and take it one day at a time.
Yeah, one step at a time. Thanks again for listening.
Anytime, Sarah. Take care and keep in touch.
Hey, thanks for being here. I just felt like talking.
Of course, Sarah. I'm always here to listen. What's been going on?
Well, I started attending this local art class recently to improve my painting skills.
That's great! I remember how much you enjoyed painting. How is the class going so far?
It’s been nice meeting new people who share the same interest. But, I feel a bit out of place sometimes.
I can understand that. It can be tough to find your footing in a new group. What's making you feel out of place?
I guess it's just that everyone seems so confident and talented. I doubt my own skills compared to them.
It's natural to feel that way in a new environment. Remember, you're there to learn and grow. Everyone starts somewhere.
Yeah, you're right. It's just that old feeling of inadequacy creeping back in, like when I received that feedback at work.
I recall you mentioning that. It sounds like it's been a recurring theme for you. Have you talked to your therapist about these feelings?
I have, actually. They've recommended mindfulness exercises to help manage my anxiety and self-doubt.
That's a good step. Have you been able to incorporate those exercises into your routine?
Trying to, but it's challenging with everything else going on, like the tensions with Jack and work stress.
How are things with Jack lately? Have you both had a chance to talk about the future?
Not really. We decided to take a break after our last argument. It's tough, but I think it might be what we need.
That sounds like a difficult decision. But it takes courage to do what's best for you both. How are you feeling about it?
I'm sad, but also a bit relieved. I guess I need to really focus on myself right now.
Taking time for yourself is important. You've been through a lot and deserve some peace and self-care.
Thanks. I just need to hold onto that thought, especially when things get overwhelming.
You can do this, Sarah. You're taking all the right steps, and your passion for painting is a wonderful outlet.
Thank you. It really helps to hear that. I'll keep trying to find balance.
You're stronger than you think. I'm here whenever you need to talk or just need someone to listen.
I appreciate that more than I can say. I really needed this conversation.
Anytime, Sarah. You're never alone in this.

turns.text: Hey Kelly, how are you doing today?
Hey, to be honest, I'm struggling a bit.
I'm here to listen. Do you want to share what's been challenging for you?
It's my thesis. I had a setback recently, and it's just really bringing me down.
I can imagine that must be tough. What happened with your thesis?
I got some feedback that I wasn't expecting. It made me realize there's a lot more work to do than I thought.
That sounds overwhelming. It can be really hard to digest unexpected feedback.
Exactly. I was feeling quite confident before, and now I just feel lost.
It's okay to feel that way. Remember, feedback is part of the process. How are you managing these feelings?
Not too well, honestly. I've been pretty demotivated and haven't been able to get much done.
It's understandable to feel stuck. Sometimes taking a step back can help. Have you tried taking a break from it all?
I've tried, but it's hard not to think about it. It feels like I'm letting myself down.
You're not letting yourself down. You're doing your best under challenging circumstances. Remember when your friend mentioned overcoming similar doubts in his studies?
Oh yeah, he struggled with something similar and he got through it. It took him a bit of time though.
Exactly. Maybe his story can be a reminder that it's possible to bounce back. Have you reached out to your friends recently?
Not recently. Maybe I should. Talking to someone who understands might help.
That sounds like a great idea. And remember, I'm always here for you too. You have support.
Thanks, I really appreciate that. It does help to know I'm not alone in this.
You definitely aren't alone. How about focusing on one small step you can take today?
Maybe I can start by reviewing the feedback more calmly, with a fresh perspective.
That sounds like a constructive plan. Taking it step by step and being kind to yourself on the journey can make a big difference.
I’ll try to keep that in mind. Thank you for listening and helping me process things.
Anytime, Kelly. You’ve got this, even if it doesn’t feel like it right now. Keep reaching out, okay?
I will. Thanks again.
Hello
Hi, how are you feeling today?
I'm feeling a bit confused and anxious.
okay, that is valid, do you have an idea what is causing the confusion?

So I've been dating and my parents are aware. But recently after I said I want to go on a trip with my boyfriend, my parents have all sorts of opinions about it. And all their traditional beliefs that I did not know existed are now on the surface and they are kinda forcing me to follow it.
For say they think "bad types of woman" go on trips with their boyfriends and I need to save myself.
They have been guilt tripping me and I feel very confused.
Your feelings are valid and it is okay to feel confused in this situation considering you love your boyfriend and parents
Have you tried discussing with your boyfriend to talk to your parents as a means of reassuring them?
Or getting someone neutral that your parents trust to talk to them?

I have. It's been a long stressful month of discussion. The problem is I don't share their beliefs, and I haven't been really "saving myself". I'm been living away from them for collage quite a while and I've been basically doing stuff that if they found out they would be very upset about.

I get how difficult and upsetting this situation is to you, i have been in a similar situation, however, in my case i took charge of my life, though they are my parents i did what i felt is good for me

I'm 26
And I see what you're saying.

I never had a voice for myself. They basically bullied and forced me to do what they wanted.
